explanations.explanation: Swarms of locusts, yes. Amos says the Lord GOD "…was preparing swarms of locusts just after the king’s harvest, as the late spring crop was coming up." (Amos 7:1) The timing is the sting here. The crop is just coming up, and that's when the locusts show up.

No flood in this vision. Amos says the Lord GOD "…was preparing swarms of locusts…" (Amos 7:1). Water is a fair guess when a crop is in danger, but this one flies in. Locusts are the answer, and they come right as the late spring crop is coming up.

Frogs are a real Bible plague, so I see where that came from. They hopped through Egypt in Exodus 8:6. But Amos sees something different: "…swarms of locusts…" (Amos 7:1). Same idea of a creature swarm, different creature, and these ones come for the crop.
True. When the locusts have eaten every green plant in the land, Amos says, "Lord GOD, please forgive!" (Amos 7:2) He doesn't wait around or argue. He speaks up for the people right away.
This one is true, friend. Once the locusts have eaten every green plant in the land, Amos says, "Lord GOD, please forgive!" (Amos 7:2) He asks for forgiveness. He doesn't stay quiet about it.

Jacob is so small, exactly. Amos asks, "How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" (Amos 7:2) That's his whole case, short and simple. I wish I could make my case that tight when I'm asking for one more cookie.

Allies never come up. Amos gives one reason, and it's about size: "How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" (Amos 7:2) Jacob is another name for Israel (Genesis 32:28). The answer is that Jacob is so small.

Rain isn't mentioned here. Amos asks, "How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" (Amos 7:2) The locusts have already eaten every green plant, so I can see why you'd think of the land's needs. But his reason is that Jacob is so small.
Not quite. The text says, "So the LORD relented from this plan." (Amos 7:3) Then He says, "It will not happen…" The locust plan does not go ahead. Amos asked, and the LORD answered.
False is right. The text says, "So the LORD relented from this plan." (Amos 7:3) Then He says, "It will not happen…" The locust plan does not go ahead. Amos speaks, and the LORD relents.

Other way around, friend. The fire doesn't stop at a small corner. Amos says it "…consumed the great deep and devoured the land." (Amos 7:4) That's the deep waters and the land, so nothing small about it.
False, and not by a little. Amos says the fire "…consumed the great deep and devoured the land." (Amos 7:4) It's not a corner of the land. It reaches the great deep and the land itself.

explanations.answer: He asks the Lord GOD to stop
explanations.explanation: He asks the Lord GOD to stop. Amos says, "Lord GOD, please stop! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" (Amos 7:5) Same worry as the first vision, and same move. He goes straight to the Lord GOD and speaks up for Jacob.

explanations.answer: He runs back home to Tekoa
explanations.explanation: Running home isn't in the text. Amos says, "Lord GOD, please stop!" (Amos 7:5) I'd have been halfway to the door, honestly. Amos speaks up for Jacob instead.

explanations.answer: He waits for the fire to pass
explanations.explanation: No waiting around here. Amos speaks right up: "Lord GOD, please stop! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" (Amos 7:5) The fire has consumed the great deep and devoured the land, and Amos asks the Lord GOD to stop.

It will not happen either. The text says, "So the LORD relented from this plan." Then the Lord GOD says, "It will not happen either…" (Amos 7:6) The word "either" matters. It's the second time the LORD relents after Amos speaks.

explanations.answer: It will burn for seven days
explanations.explanation: Seven days isn't in the text. The Lord GOD says, "It will not happen either…" (Amos 7:6) The fire doesn't burn for a week or for a day. After Amos asks, the LORD relents.
Judah never comes up in this answer. The Lord GOD says, "It will not happen either…" (Amos 7:6) He doesn't say who gets spared. He says the fire isn't going to happen.
Among His people Israel, yes. The Lord says, "I am setting a plumb line among My people Israel…" (Amos 7:8) Notice the words "My people." The plumb line is set right in the middle of them.

Gath is a swing and a miss. The Lord says, "I am setting a plumb line among My people Israel…" (Amos 7:8) He says "My people," so this one isn't about outsiders. I think that makes it hit closer to home.

The wall in the vision is where the Lord stands (Amos 7:7), so I get the pull toward walls. But the Lord says where the plumb line goes: "…among My people Israel…" (Amos 7:8) It's about the people, not Jerusalem's walls.
This time it goes the other way. The Lord says, "I will no longer spare them…" (Amos 7:8) The first two visions ended with the LORD relenting. This one doesn't.

False, and it's a big change from the first two visions. The Lord says, "I will no longer spare them…" (Amos 7:8) Twice the LORD relented after Amos spoke up (Amos 7:3, 6). Here He says no more sparing.
Deserted. The Lord says, "The high places of Isaac will be deserted…" (Amos 7:9) That's the first thing on His list. They'll sit empty, like a bakery with the lights off and nobody inside.
Rebuilt would be good news, and that's not what the Lord says. He says, "The high places of Isaac will be deserted…" (Amos 7:9) After the plumb line, the word is about emptiness, not rebuilding.

Crowded is the opposite of what the Lord says. "The high places of Isaac will be deserted…" (Amos 7:9) Crowded would be a packed house, and this is an empty one. Nobody's showing up, not even somebody pretending to be busy.

Sword. The Lord says, "…I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with My sword." (Amos 7:9) Watch how it gets personal. First the high places, then the sanctuaries, and now a house with a name on it.
A storm would fit the fire and locusts, but that isn't the word. The Lord says, "…I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with My sword." (Amos 7:9) Sword is the word for Jeroboam's house.
A staff sounds gentler, but that isn't the word. The Lord says, "…I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with My sword." (Amos 7:9) It's a sword, and it's aimed at the house of Jeroboam.
